6	# Project and User wide memories
7	
8	## Goal
9	A person working with the agent repeats themselves: the same correction, the same standing constraint, the same environment quirk, in every new session, because nothing a session learns outlives it. Memories give those notes a home — a short note on one thing, kept either for this project or for the person across every project, written when the person settles something and in hand at the start of the next session. They are working notes about how to work here, not product intent: anything that says what the product does still belongs in the docs and the specs. Memories are kept in Claude Code's memory files, so a session on the Claude Agent SDK reads them natively and a session on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint reaches the same notes through the agent's memory tools.
10	
11	## Remembering what the person settled
12	During a session the agent notices something that will matter again and writes it down.
13	- **Written on a correction or a standing rule**: the agent records a memory when the person corrects it or states something that holds beyond the task in hand, and at no other time.
14	  - **Single-use fact**: something that matters only for the current task, such as a value it just worked out or the file it is about to edit, is not remembered.
15	- **One note per memory**: a memory is one note of a few lines, named by what it is about, and carries one line of its own in the memory index.
16	- **Project or user scope**: a memory about this codebase or its environment is kept for the project, and one about how the person wants to be worked with is kept for the person across every project.
17	  - **Scope named by the person**: when the person says which scope a memory belongs to, that is where it is kept.
18	  - **One memory file for the person**: a memory kept for the person is a line in the person's own instructions file, not a scope of its own notes, since that file already follows them to every project.
19	- **The write is shown in chat**: each memory written appears in the chat as one line naming the memory and its scope, so the person can have it taken back in the same turn.
20	- **Contradicting memory is replaced**: a new memory that contradicts one already kept at the same scope replaces that one instead of being kept beside it.
21	- **Intent is filed rather than remembered**: something that says what the product does, or is a decision about it, is written to the unfiled decisions instead of being kept as a memory (docs/intent/agent.md#Unfiled decisions).
22	- **Memories stay out of the repository**: memories are kept with the person's own files rather than in the workspace's source, and a note the whole team should follow is offered as a docs change instead.
23	- **Index cap**: a scope holds at most fifty memories; a write past the cap drops the oldest note of that scope and says so in the chat line.
24	
25	## Starting a session with what is already known
26	- **Every session that may read the code starts with the memories**: every session but the blind planner begins with the project's and the person's memory index in hand.
27	- **The blind planner gets none**: a feature-planning session is given no memories (docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 1: Feature planning).
28	- **Index first and note on demand**: a session starts with the one-line index only and reads a note's body when the work touches it.
29	  - **Memory written mid-session**: a memory written during a session is in hand for the rest of that session through the write itself, which says what was remembered, while the memory index the session started with stays as it was.
30	- **Project over user on a clash**: where a project memory and a user memory say different things about the same subject, the project memory holds (docs/settings.md#Instruction files and skills).
31	- **Same memories on both engines**: a session on the Claude Agent SDK and a session on the own loop work from the same memory notes (docs/intent/agent.md#Engines).
32	  - **No second copy on the Claude engine**: memories the Claude engine reads for itself are not put in front of it again, while the person's own memories are put in front of it the same way as on the own loop (docs/settings.md#Instruction files and skills).
33	
34	## Reviewing and forgetting

36	- **Forgetting removes the note and its line**: when the person asks for a memory to be forgotten, the note and its index line go, and no later session sees it.
37	- **Notes are the truth**: when the index and the notes disagree, because the person added, changed or deleted a note by hand, the index is rebuilt from the notes.
38	- **A wrong memory is corrected where it misleads**: memories are never swept for staleness; one that turns out to be wrong is replaced at the moment it misleads a session.

1	import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
2	import { readdir, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
3	import { homedir } from 'node:os'
4	import { basename, isAbsolute, join, resolve, sep } from 'node:path'
5	import type { PostToolUseOutcome, SessionHooks, ToolUse } from '../session/hooks'
6	import { readOptional } from '../workspace-files'
7	
8	export type MemoryScope = 'project' | 'user'
9	
10	/** A scope holds at most this many notes; a write past it drops the oldest. */
11	export const MEMORY_CAP = 50
12	
13	const INDEX_FILE = 'MEMORY.md'
14	const MEMORIES_HEADING = /^##\s+Memories\s*$/
15	const MEMORY_BULLET = /^-\s+\*\*(.+?)\*\*:\s*(.*)$/
16	
17	/** Claude Code's own name for a checkout: its path with every separator turned into a dash. */
18	function sanitizedWorkspace(cwd: string): string {
19	  return cwd
20	    .split('')
21	    .map((ch) => (ch === '/' || ch === '\\' || ch === ':' ? '-' : ch))
22	    .join('')
23	}
24	
25	/**
26	 * Project notes sit beside Claude Code's own per-project memory, under the
27	 * person's home directory rather than the checkout, so they never land in a
28	 * commit and a plain Claude Code session on this project finds the same folder.
29	 */
30	export function projectMemoryDir(cwd: string, home: string = homedir()): string {
31	  return join(home, '.claude', 'projects', sanitizedWorkspace(cwd), 'memory')
32	}
33	
34	/**
35	 * User notes fold into the person's own instructions file instead of a folder
36	 * of their own: it is the one file Claude Code already reads on every project,
37	 * on both engines, so a memory that should follow the person everywhere has
38	 * nowhere else to earn that for free.
39	 */
40	export function userMemoryFile(home: string = homedir()): string {
41	  return join(home, '.claude', 'CLAUDE.md')
42	}
43	
44	export type MemoryEntry = { title: string; file: string; summary: string }
45	export type DroppedNote = { title: string; file: string }
46	
47	/** The note's title: its `# Heading`, or the file name read back as words when a note has none. */
48	function titleOf(body: string, fileName: string): string {
49	  const heading = /^#\s+(.+)$/m.exec(body)
50	  if (heading) return heading[1]!.trim()
51	  return fileName.replace(/\.md$/, '').replace(/[-_]+/g, ' ').trim()
52	}
53	
54	/** The note's one-line summary: its first non-empty line after the title. */
55	function summaryOf(body: string): string {
56	  const lines = body.split(/\r?\n/).map((l) => l.trim())
57	  const afterHeading = /^#\s+/.test(lines[0] ?? '') ? lines.slice(1) : lines
58	  return afterHeading.find((l) => l.length > 0) ?? ''
59	}
60	
61	/**
62	 * Notes are the source of truth for a project's memory: the index is always
63	 * rebuilt from the note files on disk, oldest first by when a note was last
64	 * written, so a note rewritten under the same name moves to the front and the
65	 * scope's cap is enforced by dropping whichever note has sat longest untouched.
66	 */
67	export async function rebuildProjectIndex(dir: string): Promise<{ entries: MemoryEntry[]; dropped: DroppedNote[] }> {
68	  if (!existsSync(dir)) return { entries: [], dropped: [] }
69	  const names = (await readdir(dir)).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.md') && f !== INDEX_FILE)
70	  const notes = await Promise.all(
71	    names.map(async (name) => ({ name, mtime: (await stat(join(dir, name))).mtimeMs, body: await readFile(join(dir, name), 'utf8') })),
72	  )
73	  notes.sort((a, b) => a.mtime - b.mtime)
74	  const dropped: DroppedNote[] = []
75	  while (notes.length > MEMORY_CAP) {
76	    const oldest = notes.shift()!
77	    dropped.push({ title: titleOf(oldest.body, oldest.name), file: oldest.name })
78	    await rm(join(dir, oldest.name))
79	  }
80	  const entries = notes.map(({ name, body }) => ({ title: titleOf(body, name), file: name, summary: summaryOf(body) }))
81	  const index = entries.map((e) => `- [${e.title}](${e.file}) \u2014 ${e.summary}`).join('\n')
82	  await writeFile(join(dir, INDEX_FILE), entries.length ? index + '\n' : '', 'utf8')
83	  return { entries, dropped }
84	}
85	
86	/** Where the `## Memories` section of a user-memory file sits: its heading line and the line after its last bullet. */
87	function memoriesSection(lines: string[]): { start: number; end: number } | undefined {
88	  const start = lines.findIndex((l) => MEMORIES_HEADING.test(l.trim()))
89	  if (start === -1) return undefined
90	  let end = lines.length
91	  for (let i = start + 1; i < lines.length; i++) {
92	    if (/^##\s+/.test(lines[i]!.trim())) {
93	      end = i
94	      break
95	    }
96	  }
97	  return { start, end }
98	}
99	
100	/**
101	 * Keeps the person's `## Memories` section to the same rules as a project's
102	 * notes: a title written again replaces the earlier bullet of that title
103	 * rather than sitting beside it, and the section holds at most fifty bullets,
104	 * the oldest dropped past that. A file with no such section is left alone.
105	 */
106	export function enforceUserMemoryCap(text: string): { text: string; dropped: string[]; changed: boolean } {
107	  const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/)
108	  const section = memoriesSection(lines)
109	  if (!section) return { text, dropped: [], changed: false }
110	  const { start, end } = section
111	  const bulletLines = lines.slice(start + 1, end).filter((l) => MEMORY_BULLET.test(l.trim()))
112	  const titleOfLine = (l: string): string => MEMORY_BULLET.exec(l.trim())![1]!
113	  const lastIndex = new Map<string, number>()
114	  bulletLines.forEach((l, i) => lastIndex.set(titleOfLine(l), i))
115	  const deduped = bulletLines.filter((l, i) => lastIndex.get(titleOfLine(l)) === i)
116	  const dropped: string[] = []
117	  while (deduped.length > MEMORY_CAP) dropped.push(titleOfLine(deduped.shift()!))
118	  if (dropped.length === 0 && deduped.length === bulletLines.length) return { text, dropped: [], changed: false }
119	  const rebuilt = [lines[start]!, '', ...deduped, '']
120	  return { text: [...lines.slice(0, start), ...rebuilt, ...lines.slice(end)].join('\n'), dropped, changed: true }
121	}
122	
123	/**
124	 * The person's whole `## Memories` section, exactly as it reads in their
125	 * instructions file. A user-scope memory is that one bullet line and nothing
126	 * more, so there is no separate body to read later: the section is already
127	 * the complete index.
128	 */
129	export function userMemorySection(text: string): string | undefined {
130	  const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/)
131	  const section = memoriesSection(lines)
132	  if (!section) return undefined
133	  const body = lines.slice(section.start, section.end)
134	  if (!body.some((l) => MEMORY_BULLET.test(l.trim()))) return undefined
135	  return body.join('\n').trim()
136	}
137	
138	/** The title a bullet write names, read from the tool's own text rather than re-reading the file, since the hook runs right after the write. */
139	function writtenBulletTitle(tool: ToolUse): string | undefined {
140	  const input = (typeof tool.input === 'object' && tool.input !== null ? tool.input : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
141	  const text = typeof input['new_string'] === 'string' ? input['new_string'] : typeof input['content'] === 'string' ? input['content'] : ''
142	  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
143	    const m = MEMORY_BULLET.exec(line.trim())
144	    if (m) return m[1]
145	  }
146	  return undefined
147	}
148	
149	function chatLine(scope: MemoryScope, title: string, dropped: string[]): string {
150	  const lines = [`Tell the person, as a line of your reply: "Noted for ${scope}: ${title}."`]
151	  if (dropped.length > 0) {
152	    const names = dropped.map((d) => `"${d}"`).join(', ')
153	    const plural = dropped.length > 1
154	    lines.push(`A scope keeps at most fifty notes; the oldest ${plural ? 'notes' : 'note'} (${names}) ${plural ? 'were' : 'was'} dropped to make room \u2014 say that too.`)
155	  }
156	  return lines.join(' ')
157	}
158	
159	/**
160	 * After a memory is written, rebuilds the project's index or caps the user's
161	 * Memories section, and hands the model the exact line to tell the person, so
162	 * every write reaches the chat the same way.
163	 */
164	export class MemoryContract implements SessionHooks {
165	  constructor(
166	    private readonly cwd: string,
167	    private readonly home: string = homedir(),
168	  ) {}
169	
170	  async postToolUse(tool: ToolUse & { output: string; isError: boolean }): Promise<PostToolUseOutcome> {
171	    if (tool.isError || (tool.toolName !== 'Write' && tool.toolName !== 'Edit')) return undefined
172	    const input = (typeof tool.input === 'object' && tool.input !== null ? tool.input : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
173	    const raw = input['file_path']
174	    if (typeof raw !== 'string') return undefined
175	    const path = isAbsolute(raw) ? raw : resolve(this.cwd, raw)
176	
177	    const dir = projectMemoryDir(this.cwd, this.home)
178	    if (path.startsWith(dir + sep)) {
179	      const name = basename(path)
180	      if (name === INDEX_FILE) return undefined
181	      const { entries, dropped } = await rebuildProjectIndex(dir)
182	      const written = entries.find((e) => e.file === name)
183	      const title = written?.title ?? titleOf((await readOptional(path)) ?? '', name)
184	      return { additionalContext: chatLine('project', title, dropped.map((d) => d.title)) }
185	    }
186	
187	    if (path === userMemoryFile(this.home)) {
188	      const text = await readOptional(path)
189	      if (text === undefined) return undefined
190	      const { text: capped, dropped, changed } = enforceUserMemoryCap(text)
191	      if (changed) await writeFile(path, capped, 'utf8')
192	      const title = writtenBulletTitle(tool)
193	      if (!title && dropped.length === 0) return undefined
194	      return { additionalContext: chatLine('user', title ?? 'the change above', dropped) }
195	    }
196	    return undefined
197	  }
198	}
199	
200	/** What to tell the model about writing memories, in one place so both engines read the same words. */
201	export function memoryWritingInstructions(cwd: string, home: string = homedir()): string {
202	  const dir = projectMemoryDir(cwd, home)
203	  const file = userMemoryFile(home)
204	  return [
205	    'When the person corrects you, or states something that holds beyond the task in hand, write it down as a memory so the next session already knows it; a value you just worked out or the file you are about to edit is a single-use fact, not a memory.',
206	    `A memory is one short note, a few lines, named by what it is about. One about this codebase or how it is run belongs to the project: write \`${join(dir, '<title-as-a-slug>.md')}\`, starting with "# Title" then the note \u2014 its index is rebuilt for you from the notes that exist, so only the note file itself needs writing. One about how the person wants to be worked with, across every project, belongs to them: add or replace a "- **Title**: note" line under a "## Memories" heading in \`${file}\` (add the heading yourself if it is missing). When the person names the scope, use that one, not your own guess. Writing a note or a bullet under a title already used replaces the old one instead of sitting beside it; a scope keeps at most fifty.`,
207	    'Say so in the chat as one line naming the memory and its scope, so the person can have it taken back in the same turn.',
208	    'A memory is about working here, not about the product: something that says what the product does belongs with the unfiled decisions instead, not here. A note the whole team should follow, not just you working here, is offered as a docs change instead.',
209	  ].join('\n')
210	}
